title: Plan your analytics before you build
summary: Decide what data you need to measure success before the code is written. Adding tracking afterwards is slower, and you lose the baseline you need to prove the change worked.

beginner: Start from your success metrics and guardrails. For each, ask: what user actions do we need to record to calculate it?
List those actions as events with clear names, such as 'Order Completed', and the details each needs, such as order value.
Check what is already tracked so you do not duplicate it.
Check with your privacy or legal colleague that you are not collecting personal data you do not need.
Add the tracking work to the user stories so it is built and tested with the feature.
After release, check the events arrive correctly before relying on them.
intermediate: Map each metric to the events and properties needed.
Write a tracking plan with naming conventions and owners.
Review for privacy and add tracking to story acceptance criteria.
Validate the data in a test environment and after release.
experienced: Maintain one shared tracking plan so teams use consistent definitions.
Design events around user intent so they stay useful as the interface changes.
Build data quality checks so broken tracking is caught within a day.
Plan the experiment and attribution needs up front.

canDelegateTo.task: Write the tracking plan and check the data after release
Add the events and check they fire correctly

toolExamples.ga4: Plan custom events and parameters, and check them in DebugView before release.
toolExamples.amplitude: Use the data planning features to define events so unplanned ones are flagged.
toolExamples.mixpanel: Use Lexicon to document each event so everyone reads the data the same way.
toolExamples.jira: Add 'events fire as described in the tracking plan' to the acceptance criteria.

definitionOfDone: Every success metric mapped to events
Tracking included in stories and checked after release
pitfalls: Vague event names that mean different things to different people
Collecting personal data you do not need
